title: "Simon, Beware! the Savior Said
description: "Simon, Beware! the Savior Said in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 108, “The believer's danger, safety, and duty. Lk 22:31,32”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "Si-mon, be-ware! the Sa-vior said, Sa-tan, your sub-tle foe, Al-rea-dy has his mea-sures laid Your soul to ov-er-throw.

lines: He wants to sift you all, as wheat,
But I his malice will defeat,
This warning has to you a voice,
He will support in time of need,
Yet, let us not the warning slight,
Though faith cannot be slain in fight,
While Satan watches, dare we sleep?
But, Lord, do thou the city keep,
Or else we watch in vain.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
